item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung’s 36-year-old gender minister nominee stepped down before gaining confirmation of her position amid a public backlash over her suitability for the job in the latest negative fallout from the president’s cabinet reshuffle. Yong Hye-in, a lawmaker of the minor Basic Income Party, pulled out of consideration for the position on Sunday after controversy erupted over her insistence that she would not give up her parliamentary seat while serving in the... item.title: 'Everyone's been bugging me': Trump to remove 10% duty on Irish whiskey
item.description: During the trophy presentation at the Irish Open, US President Donald Trump dropped a significant announcement: he plans to abolish the 10% tariff on Irish whiskey. This action responds to ongoing pleas from Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin and the golfing community. The Distilled Spirits Council of the United States views this as a welcomed change that will positively impact businesses and consumers in the upcoming holiday period. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Malaysia haj fund scandal: ex-religious minister denies role in US$211 million transfer
item.description: A former Malaysian religious affairs minister pleaded not guilty on Monday to three charges involving more than 860 million ringgit (US$211 million) in transactions linked to the country’s state-run haj savings fund and a Saudi property group. Jamil Khir Baharom, 65, served as minister in the Prime Minister’s Department overseeing religious affairs from 2009 until 2018, when the government of former prime minister Najib Razak lost power. item.title: Rise in abuse of election candidates is ‘changing politics’ in England
item.description: Electoral Commission finds abuse, particularly of women, minority ethnic and disabled people, is affecting candidates’ behaviour Abuse and intimidation of election candidates is “a serious and growing concern”, the Electoral Commission has said, as a review of this year’s local and mayoral elections in England revealed a surge in threats to those who stood. More than half of the candidates for Labour or Reform UK reported abuse while those most likely to be targeted were women, people from minority ethnic backgrounds and those with disabilities. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Trump says he will consider releasing 9/11 records after families request
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday said he will look into requests from families of September 11 victims to release records that could shed light on Saudi Arabia’s alleged role in the attacks 25 years ago. Several families have long alleged that a group of extremist religious leaders in Saudi Arabia gained influence in the Saudi government and aided the hijackers. Fifteen of the 19 hijackers were Saudis but the Saudi government has long denied any involvement in the attacks. The families have... Publicado también por: South China Morning Post. Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.description: Three people were killed and 15 others wounded as gunfire erupted hours before the polls opened on Monday in a semi-autonomous Muslim region of the Philippines set to choose its first elected parliament. The vote is the culmination of an on-off peace process that began in the late 1990s and established the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao in the country’s far south. A decisão intensifica a disputa entre ministros sobre o acesso ao material. André Mendonça se opõe à divulgação, alegando risco à investigação. A PF informou ao presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, que pode fornecer cópias a qualquer ministro. Gilmar Mendes, Zanin e Alexandre de Moraes pressionam pelo acesso antes da sessão de terça-feira, que analisará conversas atribuídas a Vorcaro e Moraes.
